answer: Because the nebula salt is published after the bridge checkpoint, the umber audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 128 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. An operator running 119 keys therefore pays for 119 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
